chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who made a will, and his heirs were the witnesses, so they validated it. When the man died, they annulled the will. Is it for them to reject what they acknowledged? He said: 'It is not for them to do so; the will is binding upon them if they acknowledged it during his lifetime.'
ai.seo_question: Can heirs annul a will if they witnessed and validated it while the testator was alive?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the principle of *istiqra'* (consistency) in inheritance law, specifically addressing the scenario where heirs serve as witnesses to a will. The Imam establishes that their acknowledgment during the testator's lifetime creates a binding obligation, preventing them from later revoking the bequest after death, thereby protecting the testator's intent from the heirs' potential greed. This ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on the validity of oral or witnessed declarations made in the presence of the dying person.
